hypotheses.subject: 9f4c1e7b2a3d5c8e1f0b6a4d2c9e7b5a3f1d8c6e
hypotheses.summary: A deploy of io-shop revision 9f4c1e7b2a3d5c8e1f0b6a4d2c9e7b5a3f1d8c6e at 14:14Z is the only recorded change to the service in over three months, and latency began degrading in the very next minute (p95 220ms -> 900ms -> 1800ms -> 5000ms timeouts), so the new revision almost certainly introduced the latency/timeout regression.

supporting_evidence.claim: Every recorded change to io-shop from 2026-06-01T00:00:00Z to 2026-09-17T14:17:22Z — only the 14:14:00Z deploy is listed; no other change, and no feature-flag toggle, appears in a 3.5-month lookback.
2026-09-17T14:16:00Z WARN io-shop: p95 latency at 1800ms, up from a 220ms baseline
metrics bucket {"bucket_id": "2026-09-17T14:14:00Z", "error_rate": 0.01, "p95_ms": 220} is the last healthy minute, immediately preceding the deploy's effect

hypotheses.summary: Alternative: no change caused it — the degradation could be an external/dependency slowdown (saturation, downstream I/O stall) that coincided with the deploy. The logs only record latency climbing and 5000ms timeouts with slightly falling request volume, and name no code path, dependency or flag, so a non-change cause cannot be excluded.

supporting_evidence.claim: Logs over 13:46Z-14:17:22Z contain only generic lines: 'WARN io-shop: p95 latency climbing', 'ERROR io-shop: request timeout after 5000ms' — no stack trace, error class, dependency name or flag name.
request_volume falls 1150 -> 1120 -> 1090 -> 1050 while latency rises, consistent with saturation/back-pressure rather than a specific code fault
